core_idea: Underdevelopment is not an early stage that every country passes through. It was produced by the way peripheral economies were tied to wealthy core economies through colonial history, trade and investment. Surplus flows from 'satellites' to 'metropoles', so the same process develops one and underdevelops the other.
key_concepts_note: Use the concepts already stored for this theory in the library (theories.concepts).
when_to_use: Why do some regions remain dependent on raw-material exports, remittances or aid?
How do historical and global economic ties shape a country's development options?
Typical data: historical and economic data, trade and investment flows, policy documents, comparative case studies.
common_mistakes: Treating dependency theory as one theory. Frank and Cardoso & Faletto disagree on whether development is possible under dependency.
Ignoring internal factors such as the state, class alliances and local elites.
Asserting dependency without historical and economic evidence.
